Repo: GitHub - angusmcleod/discourse-events

This plugin allows you to associate datetime ranges with topics and list those topics in the chronological order of their datetime ranges. In other words, it lets you manage events in Discourse.

You can see an example of it in my sandbox.

Note:

  • Another plugin that allows you to manage datetimes in Discourse, with more of a focus on timezone management, is Discourse Chronos (when it is released).

  • If you’re managing events being held at physical locations, you may want to consider using this plugin alongside my Locations Plugin (both are in action in the ‘Events’ category in my sandbox).

Features:

  • Events can be turned on for specific categories by toggling ‘Allow events to be added to topics in this category’ in the Category settings.

  • When events are turned on for a Category:

    • The composer will include an ‘Add Date and Time’ button when composing a new topic in that category.

    • This opens a modal that allows you to add a start datetime and an end datetime

      Screen Shot 2017-09-11 at 9.31.18 AM.png710x436 28.1 KB

      Time selection is aided by a dropdown with 30 minute increments. Date selection is aided by a calendar picker.

    • ‘Agenda’ will be added to the category nav items. It can be selected as the default list for the category in the category settings. This list filter will display a list of the topics with datetime ranges associated with them in the ascending chronological order (i.e. earliest first) of the start datetime for each range.

      Screen Shot 2017-09-11 at 9.44.59 AM.png1126x311 37 KB

      The other lists in the category will be ordered as normal.

      Screen Shot 2017-09-11 at 9.46.51 AM.png1128x365 43.3 KB

  • When an event is added to a topic:

    • The event details will appear underneath the topic title.

    • If the events add to calendar site setting is turned on, an ‘Add to Calendar’ button will appear to the right of the event details. This provides a direct link to add the event to Google calendar and allows the user to download an .ics file with the event details.

Admin settings:

  • events add to calendar: This toggles the ‘Add to Calendar’ button next to the event details in the topic.

More Dev notes:

  • Datetimes are stored as Unix timestamps (i.e seconds since epoch). This makes it easy to order the topics using the existing topic list filter structure.

  • Time conversion and formatting on the client is handled by moment.js; see e.g. the eventLabel helper. Should probably add settings that allow the time format to be set.

  • Time selection dropdown is handled by the jquery-timepicker plugin. Probably could be replaced by a native solution in the future. And the increment period of the times in the dropdown should be a setting.

  • As raised re the similar button in the Locations Plugin, adding a button to the composer is perhaps not ideal. Trying to think of a better solution for this.
